KISWAHILI ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 3
SUBJECT: KISWAHILI ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Kinyume cha “refu” ni: (1 mark)
   A. pana
   B. zito
   C. nene
   D. fupi

2. When practising Hadithi, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Hadithi.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Hadithi.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Hadithi.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Hadithi.

3. When practising Msamiati, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Msamiati.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Msamiati.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Msamiati.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Msamiati.

4. When practising Masimulizi, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Masimulizi.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Masimulizi.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Masimulizi.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Masimulizi.

5. Wingi wa “mtoto” ni: (1 mark)
   A. mitoto
   B. watoto
   C. kitoto
   D. mato

6. When practising Maagano, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Maagano.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Maagano.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Maagano.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Maagano.

7. When practising Usalama, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Usalama.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Usalama.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Usalama.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Usalama.

8. When practising upatiwa kadi za nambari 51-100, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding upatiwa kadi za nambari 51-100.
   B. Use insults to “practise” upatiwa kadi za nambari 51-100.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to upatiwa kadi za nambari 51-100.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for upatiwa kadi za nambari 51-100.

9. When practising nyakati, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for nyakati.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to nyakati.
   C. Copy random text without understanding nyakati.
   D. Use insults to “practise” nyakati.

10. Ni sentensi ipi iliyo sahihi kisarufi? (1 mark)
   A. Mwanafunzi anasoma kitabu.
   B. Kitabu anasoma mwanafunzi kwa.
   C. Anasoma mwanafunzi kitabu ya.
   D. Mwanafunzi anasoma vitabu mzuri.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Masimulizi and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Dukani and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Masimulizi and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Hadithi and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — fupi

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Hadithi.

3. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Msamiati.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Masimulizi.

5. B — watoto

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Maagano.

7. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Usalama.

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for upatiwa kadi za nambari 51-100.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for nyakati.

10. A — Mwanafunzi anasoma kitabu.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Hadithi; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
